    WITH cdb_last_failed_jobs AS
(
SELECT CON_ID,
OWNER,
JOB_NAME,
MAX(ACTUAL_START_DATE) AS START_DATE
FROM CDB_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED'
GROUP BY CON_ID, OWNER, JOB_NAME
)
,
cdb_last_succeeded_jobs AS
(
SELECT CON_ID,
OWNER,
JOB_NAME,
MAX(ACTUAL_START_DATE) AS START_DATE
FROM CDB_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS
WHERE STATUS = 'SUCCEEDED'
GROUP BY CON_ID, OWNER, JOB_NAME
)
,
cdb_last_failed_jobs_with_earlier_success AS
(
SELECT cdb_last_failed_jobs.CON_ID,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.OWNER,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.JOB_NAME,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.START_DATE
FROM cdb_last_failed_jobs,
cdb_last_succeeded_jobs
WHERE cdb_last_failed_jobs.CON_ID = cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.CON_ID
AND cdb_last_failed_jobs.OWNER = cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.OWNER
AND cdb_last_failed_jobs.JOB_NAME = cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.JOB_NAME
AND cdb_last_failed_jobs.START_DATE < cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.START_DATE
)
,
cdb_last_failed_jobs_without_earlier_success AS
(
SELECT UNIQUE cdb_last_failed_jobs.CON_ID,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.OWNER,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.JOB_NAME,
cdb_last_failed_jobs.START_DATE
FROM cdb_last_failed_jobs, cdb_last_succeeded_jobs
WHERE (cdb_last_failed_jobs.CON_ID != cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.CON_ID)
OR (cdb_last_failed_jobs.OWNER != cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.OWNER)
OR (cdb_last_failed_jobs.JOB_NAME != cdb_last_succeeded_jobs.JOB_NAME)
)
,
cdb_latest_run_failed_jobs AS
(
SELECT CON_ID,
OWNER,
JOB_NAME,
START_DATE
FROM cdb_last_failed_jobs_without_earlier_success
UNION
SELECT CON_ID,
OWNER,
JOB_NAME,
START_DATE
FROM cdb_last_failed_jobs_with_earlier_success
),
cdb_final_latest_run_failed_jobs_set AS
(
SELECT CON_ID,
OWNER,
JOB_NAME,
START_DATE
FROM cdb_latest_run_failed_jobs
WHERE JOB_NAME NOT IN (SELECT JOB_NAME FROM CDB_SCHEDULER_JOBS WHERE STATE IN ('BROKEN', 'DISABLED'))
)
,
cdb_failed_count_job_set AS (
SELECT CON_ID, SUM(sub_fail_count) AS failed_count
FROM (
SELECT CON_ID, count(1) AS sub_fail_count
FROM cdb_final_latest_run_failed_jobs_set
GROUP BY CON_ID

UNION ALL

SELECT CON_ID, count(1) AS sub_fail_count
FROM CDB_JOBS WHERE (broken != 'Y' AND NVL(failures,0) > 0)
GROUP BY CON_ID
)
GROUP BY CON_ID
)
,
cdb_broken_count_job_set AS (
SELECT CON_ID, SUM(sub_broken_count) AS broken_count
FROM (
SELECT CON_ID, count(1) AS sub_broken_count
FROM CDB_SCHEDULER_JOBS
WHERE STATE = 'BROKEN'
GROUP BY CON_ID
UNION ALL
SELECT CON_ID, count(1) AS sub_broken_count
FROM CDB_JOBS
WHERE BROKEN = 'Y'
GROUP BY CON_ID
)
GROUP BY CON_ID
)
,
cdb_final_count_details AS (
SELECT F.CON_ID AS CON_ID,
NVL(F.failed_count,0) AS FAILED,
NVL(B.broken_count,0) AS BROKEN
FROM cdb_failed_count_job_set F LEFT JOIN cdb_broken_count_job_set B
ON F.CON_ID = B.CON_ID
UNION
SELECT B.CON_ID,
NVL(F.failed_count,0) AS FAILED,
NVL(B.broken_count,0) AS BROKEN
FROM cdb_broken_count_job_set B LEFT JOIN cdb_failed_count_job_set F
ON B.CON_ID = F.CON_ID
)
SELECT c.name AS pdb_name,
cdb_final_count_details.broken,
cdb_final_count_details.failed
FROM cdb_final_count_details, v$containers c
WHERE cdb_final_count_details.con_id = TO_NUMBER(c.con_id)

    with pdbview AS
(select con_id, name from v$containers where con_id != 2)
SELECT  pdb.name,
a.name "DB Name",
e.property_value "Global Name",
replace(b.banner, c.version, c.version_full) "DB Version",
c.host_name "Host Name",
c.instance_name "Instance Name" ,
to_char(c.startup_time,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') "Instance Start Time",
decode(c.logins,'RESTRICTED','YES','NO') "Restricted Mode",
a.log_mode  "Archive Log Mode" ,
case when pdb.con_id=0
then
decode(a.open_mode,'READ ONLY','YES','NO')
else
decode(vpb.OPEN_MODE,'READ ONLY','YES','NO')
end
"Read Only Mode",
nlsp1.value,
nlsp2.value,
p.property_value,
to_char(a.created,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') created,
substr(banner,instr(banner,'Oracle Database '),19) release,
nvl(trim(substr(banner,instr(banner,'Oracle Database ')+19,instr(banner,' Release') - instr(banner,'Oracle Database  ') - 19)),decode(instr(banner,'Personal'),0,'','Personal')) edition,
c.version_full dbversion,
DECODE(addr.word_len, 64, '1', '0')  is64bit,
substr(substr(banner, instr(banner, '-') + 2),
instr(substr(banner, instr(banner, '-') + 2),' ')+1)
rel_status,
a.supplemental_log_data_min  as sup_log_data_min,
case when  (select count(*) from cdb_users u where u.username ='DVSYS' and u.user_id = 1279990 and u.con_id = pdb.con_id)  > 0
then
case when (select value from v$option o where o.parameter ='Oracle Database Vault' and (o.con_id = pdb.con_id or o.con_id = 0)) ='TRUE'
then
1 -- Enabled
else
0 --Disabled
end
when (select count(*) from cdb_users u where u.username ='DVSYS' and u.user_id = 1279990 and u.con_id = pdb.con_id) = 0
then
case when (select value from v$option o where parameter ='Oracle Database Vault'  and (o.con_id = pdb.con_id or o.con_id = 0)) = 'TRUE'
then
-1 -- Not Configured
else
-2 -- Not Installed
end
end
dv_status_code

AND   p.con_id = pdb.con_id
AND   vpb.con_id(+) = pdb.con_id

          declare
         agedFileRec   dbms_rcvman.agedFileRec_t;
         first         boolean := FALSE; 
         alldest       number  := dbms_rcvman.FALSE#; 
         policy        varchar2(512); 
      begin
         if (:first > 0) then
            first := TRUE;
            if (:alldest > 0) then 
               alldest := dbms_rcvman.TRUE#; 
            end if; 
            dbms_rcvman.setRecoveryDestFile(TRUE); 
            dbms_rcvman.getRedoLogDeletionPolicy(policy  => policy); 
            dbms_rcvman.setRedoLogDeletionPolicy(policy  => policy, 
                                                 alldest => alldest); 
         end if; 
         dbms_rcvman.getAppliedAl(first => first,
                                  agedFileRec => agedFileRec);
         :type  := agedFileRec.type;
         :key   := agedFileRec.key;
      end;

          declare
         policy        varchar2(512);
         alldest       number  := dbms_rcvman.FALSE#;
         rlgscn        number; 
      begin
         if (:alldest > 0) then
            alldest := dbms_rcvman.TRUE#;
         end if;
         dbms_rcvman.setRecoveryDestFile(TRUE); 
         dbms_rcvman.getRedoLogDeletionPolicy(policy  => policy);
         dbms_rcvman.setRedoLogDeletionPolicy(policy  =>  policy,
                                              alldest =>  alldest);
         if ((policy like '%APPLIED%' OR 
              policy like '%SHIPPED%') AND 
             policy not like '%BACKED UP%') then
            dbms_rcvman.getSCNForAppliedPolicy(
               minscn     => :applied_scn
              ,rlgscn     => rlgscn);
         else
            :applied_scn := 0;
         end if;
      end;

      'startup_time' value to_char(i.startup_time, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS'),

    ),

      ),

        'utilization_pct' value (select round(100 * current_utilization / nullif(case when regexp_like(trim(limit_value), '^[0-9]+$') then to_number(trim(limit_value)) end, 0), 2) from v$resource_limit where resource_name = 'processes')
      ),
      'blocking_sessions' value (select count(*) from v$session where blocking_session is not null),
      'failed_jobs_24h' value (select count(*) from dba_scheduler_job_run_details where status = 'FAILED' and log_date >= systimestamp - interval '1' day)
    )
  ) returning clob
) from v$instance i cross join v$database d

    SELECT nonprimarydb.name as pdbName
,MAX(CASE WHEN takecdbstatus.open_mode LIKE 'MOUNT%' THEN 1
WHEN takecdbstatus.open_mode LIKE 'READ%' THEN 1
ELSE 0
END) as state_num
FROM gv$containers nonprimarydb
,gv$containers takecdbstatus
WHERE nonprimarydb.name <> 'PDB$SEED'
AND   takecdbstatus.name = 'CDB$ROOT'
AND ((sys_context('USERENV','CURRENT_USER') like 'SYS%' AND takecdbstatus.open_mode LIKE 'MOUNT%') OR (takecdbstatus.open_mode LIKE 'READ%'))
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
FROM v$database
WHERE database_role <> 'PRIMARY')
GROUP BY nonprimarydb.name
UNION ALL
SELECT primarydb.name as pdbName
,MAX(CASE WHEN primarydb.open_mode like 'READ%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as state_num
FROM gv$containers primarydb
WHERE primarydb.name <> 'PDB$SEED'
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
FROM v$database
WHERE database_role = 'PRIMARY')
GROUP BY primarydb.name

    Reading the chartsWhat each chart and glyph on this page encodes

    Band

    Dot = Current, in σ from the prior mean. Shaded = normal (±1σ, ±2σ); ticks at ±2σ and ±3σ. Filled = finding, hollow = normal; past +8σ the dot pins and prints its z.

    ▲ ×5.4▲ 22.5%▼ 4.2%

    Δ vs mean

    ×n when Current is at least twice the prior mean, else a percentage. Red or amber only on a finding.

    13-window chart

    One column per compared window, oldest left; Current last, wider, indigo. Band = normal range, line = mean, dot = finding.

    Full-span activity

    Top of every view: active sessions over the whole span as stacked areas, hourly (or the shorter cadence), by wait class and by wait event (the 14 largest, the rest as Other events); zoomed to 6 hours or less, the compared windows minute by minute. Stripes = compared windows (Current indigo, pinned amber, skipped grey). Hover for each series’ AAS, drag across either chart to zoom both, double-click to reset; a legend item hides its series, a stripe pins its window. Hover a class or event to highlight it: from the legend it is drawn from zero, its own axis; a class lights its events below. Click its band (or Shift+click the legend) to keep it, Esc clears.

    Activity per window

    Timeline Activity lane (all sessions) and the DB time card (foreground sessions only, ASH’s estimate of DB time): one stacked column per compared window, same wait classes. Current labels its two largest classes.

    Span chart

    All sections: active sessions by wait class across the whole span. Compared windows shaded, Current in indigo.

    Trend

    A table row’s windows as bars from zero, oldest left: shaded = normal range, indigo = Current. Hover a strip for the last four values and the normal range.

    Release marker

    A release or patch, on the boundary between the two windows it fell between. Its line runs down every chart.

    Step line

    Parameters and plan hashes step where the value changed. Dot = the change; labels = old and new value.

    ◆ plan changed✚ first seen▽ DOP downgrade

    Glyphs

    Drawn in the window where it happened.

    Day profile

    Last 24 h by hour vs the same hour on the prior days, one row per stat: red above, blue below (signed z). A triangle marks a flagged hour; the line chart below it plots one stat: pick it with its button (the dot and counts say how unusual its day is), a row label, or the arrow keys.

    Hover and pin

    Timeline: hover a column for its values; click a date or an ASH stripe to pin it. The gutter then compares against it (“vs 13 Aug”); Current or Esc clears it.

    About this reportMethod, sources and thresholds behind every section
    Scoring
    z = (Current − μ) ÷ max(σ, 2% of |μ|) over the prior valid windows. |z| > 3 is large, |z| > 2 moderate, else normal — but only when the move is material: |Δ| ≥ 10% and, for wait classes, ≥ 2% of the Current window’s wait time (otherwise normal, tagged immaterial). Each metric has its own direction and floors (sql/lib/metric_policy.plsql): a move in the good direction is improved, an informational counter is noted — neither is highlighted or counted. Twins (the SYSMETRIC rate of a SYSSTAT counter, the CPU half of the CPU/wait ratio) are shown muted and never counted. Fewer than 3 prior values: Δ only. |z| beyond ±99 is capped for display; σ≈0 flags a baseline that barely moved.
    Band and Δ
    The band plots Current in σ from the prior mean on one scale for the whole page (−4 to +8σ). Normal range = μ ± 2σ in the row’s own unit. Δ vs mean reads ×n at twice the mean or more, else a percentage.
    Windows
    One window per step back from 2026-09-18 12:00:00, 1h wide, every 1h A window is skipped (and dropped from every baseline) when a snapshot is missing, the begin and end snapshot are the same, the instance restarted inside it, it straddles a DBID change, or its nearest snapshot is more than 15 minutes off the window edge.
    DB time
    DB CPU (dba_hist_sys_time_model, foreground) plus non-idle wait time (dba_hist_system_event, all sessions incl. background) per snapshot interval, stacked by wait class, from the earliest compared window to Current. Not a strict foreground DB-time profile. A snapshot pair across an instance restart is a gap.
    Verdict
    One sentence from the first two finding cards (the loudest card, then DB time when it is flagged): the lead metric and its move, ×n at twice the mean or more, else a percentage. For DB time, where the extra time went: CPU vs wait from DB CPU against DB time. Likely source: a statement that ran with a new plan in the Current window, else a newcomer in the top SQL by physical reads, else a statement first seen this window, else the segment the extra reads land on. Fixed phrases, no free text.
    Finding cards
    One card per metric family of the scoring policy (sql/lib/metric_policy.plsql); families that tell one story share a card: Physical I/O (physical and logical reads, long table scans, User I/O waits), DB time (DB time, the CPU / wait ratio, response time), Network (Network waits, SQL*Net bytes), Commit (Commit waits, commits), Parsing, Writes and redo. A card is led by its loudest large, else moderate, metric of the card’s main family. Twins are folded under related metrics and never counted.
    DB time strip
    DBA_HIST_SYSSTAT DB time per compared window, divided by 100 (centiseconds per second = average active sessions); release markers sit on the boundary between the two windows they fall between.
    Checked and normal
    Every other scored metric: the normal ones, loudest first; moved, too small to matter = past |z| 2 but under the metric’s materiality floor, or an informational counter; improved = a material move in the good direction. None of them is counted.
    What changed around it
    Plan change: a statement that ran in the Current window with a plan other than the prior windows’ most frequent one (SQL Monitor). Its bars are its elapsed seconds per window from DBA_HIST_SQLSTAT; the step line is the most frequent captured plan per window, carried over windows with no capture; only the SQL Monitor max elapsed is scored. Configuration: every changed parameter as a step line.
    Evidence library
    Summary view: every other section as one row with a one-line status and its counts; open a row to read the section in place. All sections shows every section in full.
    ASH timeline
    dba_hist_active_sess_history over the full span, one scan: hourly (or the cadence) in All sections; at the top of every view (Activity, whole span) on the same grid (coarser only past 10000 buckets), by wait class and by wait event (the 14 events with the most samples, ties by name, the rest summed as Other events), plus each compared window’s own values (samples ÷ 360 ÷ window hours; overlapping windows each count a shared sample) and a 1-minute series inside the compared windows (samples ÷ 6, each minute once; at most 40000 minutes, the most recent windows first), drawn when zoomed to 6 hours or less. ON CPU is CPU in both; Idle excluded. Compared windows shaded. ASH is not scored. Each event carries its wait class from the same scan, so highlighting a class lights its events (and an event its class); a highlighted series is re-stacked from zero on its own y axis, the others faded above it.
    Timeline
    One column per compared window, one row per metric, from the same values and scoring as the tables: the headline and every flagged load / metric row, flagged wait classes and the top foreground events, the top segments and datafile by reads, the top statements by elapsed (SQL Monitor rows for a plan change or a DOP downgrade), changed parameters. Statement, segment and file rows are ranked, not scored: a plain ratio against the mean of the prior windows they made the top list in. Needs JavaScript; every number is also in All sections.
    Utilization
    Workload volume and shape (transaction, call and logon rates, session counts, data and network volume) from DBA_HIST_SYSMETRIC_SUMMARY, averaged over each window. A usage overview, not a health check: the band is drawn but never scored.
    Load profile
    DBA_HIST_SYSSTAT (end − begin snapshot) ÷ window seconds, summed across instances. Trend: per-window values as bars, oldest to Current, over the shaded normal range. Current cell bar = value ÷ row maximum.
    System metrics
    DBA_HIST_SYSMETRIC_SUMMARY averaged over each window. Rates and counters: SUM across instances per snapshot, then AVG; ratios and latencies: AVG across instances per snapshot, then AVG. Units per metric name.
    Wait events
    Foreground: DBA_HIST_SYSTEM_EVENT; background: DBA_HIST_BG_EVENT_SUMMARY. Idle excluded. Top 10 events by time waited (s) and by average latency (ms = time waited ÷ total waits); the chart stacks wait-class time per window. When five or more flagged events moved together within a narrow band, the table notes one table-wide shift and demotes large rows to moderate.
    Top SQL
    Top 10 statements per ranking and window from DBA_HIST_SQLSTAT *_DELTA columns; ranked, not scored. The bump chart draws one line per statement across the windows; Break down by re-aggregates by parsing schema, module or action.
    Top SQL ASH
    For each statement in the Top SQL pool: ASH samples per bucket split by wait event (top 7 per statement, the rest as Other; CPU = ON CPU). Statements with fewer than 5 samples are placeholders.
    SQL Monitor
    Executions persisted by SQL Monitor (DBA_HIST_REPORTS, component_name='sqlmonitor'), summaries only. Only completed, expensive-enough or parallel executions are persisted, so a statement’s absence does not mean it ran fast and row counts are not execution rates. An execution still running at the report end has no row yet. Rows are attributed to a window by execution start time. The table is scored on max elapsed time (rule above); the scatter plots every captured execution.
    Segment and file I/O
    Segments: DBA_HIST_SEG_STAT *_DELTA joined to DBA_HIST_SEG_STAT_OBJ; reads and writes in blocks, requests in I/O calls. Files: DBA_HIST_FILESTATXS / DBA_HIST_TEMPSTATXS deltas, blocks scaled to MB by block size; the file-type view is DBA_HIST_IOSTAT_FILETYPE (all database I/O, so its totals differ). Ranked, not scored; the type rollups cover all segments and files.
    Parameters
    Initialization parameters from dba_hist_parameter whose value differs across the compared windows (value as of each window’s end snapshot, lowest container wins in a CDB). Highlighted cells differ from Current; — = not present at that snapshot; (unset) = present but empty.
